identity.real_world_identity_notes: Iveco racing truck of the Brazilian Copa Truck championship, one of the manufacturers the series lists among its competitors.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled. There is no automatic cut or blip, so the driver lifts to upshift.

The gearbox is a five-speed plus a launch gear, and first is only used to pull away. A tester found first effectively unavailable in normal running and thought it a fault; it is the real specification faithfully modelled, and the six observed gears are that 5+1.

The regulations mandate a mechanically operated H-pattern manual gearbox but leave its design free, so the engagement type is not established and the downshift blip stays unknown rather than being inferred from racing practice.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.iveco-stralis.20260814t193645192z-54adb5fc by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

claims.basis: Registered sources establish the championship and its mandated gearbox, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.

The championship regulations mandate a mechanically operated H-pattern manual gearbox, and the reference gives a 5-speed plus launch gear. The live drive selected six H-pattern gears, which is that 5+1.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

driver_summary: Copa Truck regulations mandate a mechanically operated H-pattern manual, a five-speed with a launch gear. Whether it engages by dogs or synchros is not stated, so blip on downshifts to be safe.
